question: Which of the following diuretics is contraindicated in the presence of cardiac failure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Mannitol" -> "osmotic diuretic" -> "increases intravascular volume" -> "worsens cardiac workload" -> "contraindicated in cardiac failure" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Spironolactone" -> "potassium-sparing diuretic" -> "reduces aldosterone effects" -> "helps manage fluid overload in heart failure" -> "not contraindicated in cardiac failure" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Furosemide" -> "loop diuretic" -> "reduces blood volume" -> "decreases preload and cardiac workload" -> "used in management of cardiac failure" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hydrochlorothiazide" -> "thiazide diuretic" -> "reduces blood volume" -> "can be used in stable heart failure management" -> "not contraindicated in cardiac failure" -> 90%
analysis: Mannitol is contraindicated in cardiac failure due to its mechanism of increasing intravascular volume, which can exacerbate cardiac workload. This is in contrast to the other diuretics listed, which are used to manage fluid overload in heart failure.
